lines.trans: Calling camera cues accurately is important.
That camera is a Jimmy Jib.
Who is that? Somebody's there.
They aren't sleeping, though?
Who is beside her? It's Ra Joon-mo!
Didn't he say he was going to the Broadcast Commission today?
There was a rumour that the two of them are dating.
How would I know that?

examples.trans: Wait for the director's cue.
The cue just came in.
Please keep the time accurately.
Do you remember that number exactly?

meanings.note: also combines with nouns to form verbs

examples.trans: I have a lot of work to do today.
What are you doing right now?

meanings.note: bound noun, often contracted to 거 in speech
nominalizes clauses; 것이 contracts to 게

examples.trans: This is mine.
It is good to go to sleep early.
Health is the most important thing.
There is an important meeting today.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?
Please move the camera over here.
I bought a new camera.

meanings.note: broadcasting term from the Jimmy Jib crane brand

examples.trans: A Jimmy Jib is set up in the studio.
We shoot the whole stage with the Jimmy Jib.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?
There are many people here.
That person is a really good person.

meanings.en: to be (in a place); to exist; there is

examples.trans: There is coffee on the desk.
Do you have time right now?

related.gloss: to not exist; to not have

examples.trans: Did you sleep well last night?
The baby is sleeping right now.

related.gloss: to wake up; to get up

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not a holiday.
Please sit next to me.
There is a cafe next to the bank.

meanings.en: Ra Joon-mo (character name in The Producers)

examples.trans: PD Ra Joon-mo is in a meeting right now.
Ra Joon-mo is walking over there.

meanings.note: used both as a noun and adverbially without a particle

examples.trans: The weather is really nice today.
What are we eating for dinner today?
I have to attend the Broadcast Commission meeting today.
The Broadcast Commission announced new regulations.
I am going to the office right now.
Where are you going on the weekend?

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: native Korean numeral; 둘이 means 'the two of them'

examples.trans: The two of us work together.
Two coffees, please.

meanings.en: to date; to go out with (romantically)
to make friends; to associate with

examples.trans: Since when have those two been dating?
I want to make many new friends.

related.gloss: to date; to be in a relationship

examples.trans: Is that rumour true?
A strange rumour is going around the company.
I will go first.
I saw that movie too.

meanings.note: 그것을 contracts to 그걸 in speech

examples.trans: How did you know that?
That is my bag.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.
Let's meet again next time!
It started raining again.

meanings.en: to see; to look at; to watch

meanings.note: as in 또 봐요 ('see you again')

examples.trans: See you at the office tomorrow.
I watched an interesting drama yesterday.
